cells.tense: Right now you are moving on something while the road ahead is still mostly unlit.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you've been treating as undecided and take one visible step on it before the day ends.
cells.core:
You can move while the picture is still blurry. Not because you've stopped caring whether you're right — because you've noticed you don't have to see the whole road to take the next step. You decide something in the middle of not knowing and it holds. That's rarer than it sounds.

The not-knowing doesn't slow the moving down; it's what keeps the moving honest. You're not charging blind and you're not waiting for a sign. What you could feed next is somebody else's — the part of you that listens, that lets a perception land without needing to prove it first. Start there and see whether the step you already took gets sharper.
cells.sheetLine: You can act before the road is fully drawn.
cells.verb: Cutting through what's stalled by putting weight behind one clear move.
cells.place: Where the road ahead isn't fully drawn and you take the next step anyway.

cells.tense: You are pushing at a decision that hasn't finished forming and bracing for a road that hasn't appeared.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you've forced to a conclusion this week and say out loud that you don't know yet.
cells.core:
You're moving before the moment has arrived. The step comes faster than the ground under it, so you keep pushing — another decision, another boundary, another forward motion — as if enough momentum will make the road appear. What the pushing was for is getting further away the harder you push.

Nothing here is broken. The moving is just running past its own timing. What you could feed next is the depth underneath it — seeing the pattern instead of forcing the next move, understanding something well enough that the way forward stops needing to be shoved. Leave one thing genuinely open and see what the open space tells you.
cells.sheetLine: You're outrunning the road and calling it speed.
cells.verb: Cutting through what's stalled by putting weight behind one clear move.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you, moving on nothing for a while now.
cells.ask: Name one thing you've been leaving to someone else, and make one concrete choice about it today.
cells.core:
The moving has gone quiet. Where there used to be a step taken in the middle of not knowing, there's a step deferred — you wait for more clarity, more certainty, a better moment, and the waiting keeps things exactly as foggy as before. Nothing gets decided because nothing gets decided.

The ability isn't gone; it just hasn't been fed. What brings it back is a firm move on something solid, not another guess at the blurry thing. Find one real arrangement in your life you keep letting drift — a time, a commitment, a plan — and set it firmly. The clear ground gives the next step somewhere to land.

cells.tense: You are already steering through this uncertainty and describing the steering as something that happened to you.
cells.ask: Say 'I chose that' about one decision you've been calling obvious or unavoidable.
cells.core:
The pen is already moving. Look at how you handle the unlit part of the road — what you slow down for, what you speed past, which risks you'll take without checking. That's you doing it. You've been describing the whole thing as circumstance, as the situation, as what anyone would do. The deciding is happening; the naming of it isn't.

No scolding here. You've been leading through a stretch of fog and letting the fog take the credit. What comes back when you take it is simpler than authority — knowing what you released and what you kept. Name one ending you chose and acted on, and let it be yours.
